vehicles.slot: PREFERRED: Touchscreen — Settings > Vehicle > Service > Park brake release. No traditional mechanical shift lock slot. Jump terminals: remove trailer hitch cover to access the jump-start wire harness (red/black leads).
shift: PREFERRED METHOD — requires 12V power:
Turn the vehicle to ON/Ready mode.
On the touchscreen: go to Settings > Vehicle > Service.
Enable 'Park brake release' — this releases the electronic park brake so the vehicle can roll.
Press the brake pedal and confirm the electronic park brake releases.
Load the vehicle onto the flatbed — pull slowly (if you pull too fast the vehicle shifts back to Park).
Park brake release turns off automatically after 15 minutes.
DEAD BATTERY METHOD:
Jump the 12V auxiliary battery using the wire harness behind the trailer hitch cover.
Remove the trailer hitch cover (two captive flathead screws — turn quarter-turn counterclockwise).
Pull out the jump-start wire harness. Connect red (+) to red lead, black (−) to black lead.
Keep the jump source running until the Rivian displays power up.
Once powered, use the touchscreen Park brake release method above.
neutral: FLATBED ONLY — never tow with any wheels on the ground.
STEP 1: Attempt to restore 12V power first (see jump procedure in shift steps above).
STEP 2: Once powered, go to Settings > Vehicle > Service > Park brake release.
STEP 3: Load vehicle onto flatbed. If you pull the vehicle too fast it will re-engage Park automatically.
DEAD 12V — NO POWER AT ALL: Lift the rear wheels using wheel skates, a dolly, or a wheel-lift.
The electronic park brake is only on the REAR wheels — if rear wheels are lifted, the front wheels roll freely.
Secure the vehicle to the tow truck before lifting rear wheels.
NEVER attempt to tow with all four wheels on the ground — electric drivetrain will be damaged.
For trips over 50 miles: turn on Vehicle Shipping Mode (Settings > Vehicle) to preserve battery charge.
vehicles.notes: Official Rivian Tow Operator Guide (June 2024): FLATBED ONLY. No mechanical shift lock slot in passenger compartment. Jump access is via the trailer hitch wire harness, NOT the frunk. Park brake release via touchscreen is the correct procedure. Electronic park brake is rear-wheel only — lifting rear wheels allows front wheels to roll freely.
vehicles.warn: FLATBED ONLY. No mechanical shift lock override in cabin. Jump via trailer hitch harness — NOT frunk terminals. If pulled too fast onto flatbed, vehicle auto-shifts back to Park.
vehicles.towMethod: FLATBED ONLY — quad motor or dual motor AWD electric drivetrain. Never tow with any wheels on ground.
towNotes: ELECTRIC VEHICLE — FLATBED ONLY without exception.
No manual parking brake cable — must have 12V power to release parking brake.
If parking brake cannot be released: lift rear wheels with skates/dollies to move vehicle.
12V frunk battery — very accessible once front hood is open.
Heavy vehicle (Class 2b) — verify flatbed GVWR capacity.

epb.override: Restore 12V via frunk terminals. Tow Mode on touchscreen releases EPB automatically. No manual cable override.
steps: Connect jump pack to 12V frunk terminals.
Touchscreen: Service > Tow Mode. EPB releases automatically.
If Tow Mode unavailable: lift rear wheels with skates to move vehicle.

airSuspension.description: Rivian air suspension with multiple ride heights. Camp Mode, All-Terrain, etc.
towingNotes: Use standard ride height for flatbed loading.
Suspension can lower vehicle at Access Mode — useful for ramp approach.

vehicles.steeringLock: Electronic steering lock — Tow Mode on touchscreen disengages it.

battery.location: Jump access: TRAILER HITCH AREA — remove hitch cover to access jump-start wire harness. 12V auxiliary battery is inside the vehicle (under frunk liner on Gen 1; under passenger seat on Gen 2 2025+).
battery.jumpTerminals: Behind trailer hitch cover — red (+) and black (−) leads in jump-start wire harness. Gen 1 (2022-2024): battery also accessible by removing frunk liner. Gen 2 (2025+): 12V battery under passenger seat.
battery.warnings: Jump via trailer hitch harness only — do NOT use frunk terminals for jumping. Keep jump source running until vehicle fully powers up. Never touch high-voltage components (orange cables). Flatbed only.

knownIssues.title: No Mechanical Shift Lock Override in Cabin
knownIssues.detail: Unlike most vehicles, the Rivian R1T and R1S have NO mechanical shift lock slot in the passenger compartment. You cannot insert a key or screwdriver near the gear selector to release Park. The only options are: (1) restore 12V power and use Settings > Vehicle > Service > Park brake release on the touchscreen, or (2) lift the rear wheels — the electronic park brake is rear-only, so lifting the rear lets the vehicle roll onto a flatbed.

knownIssues.title: Jump Access Is at the Trailer Hitch, Not the Frunk
knownIssues.detail: The jump-start wire harness is accessed by removing the trailer hitch cover (two captive flathead screws, quarter-turn counterclockwise). Pull out the harness and connect red to red, black to black. Keep the jump source running until the vehicle fully powers on. On Gen 1 vehicles the 12V battery can also be reached by removing the frunk liner, but the hitch harness is the designed tow operator method.

knownIssues.title: Vehicle Auto-Shifts Back to Park if Pulled Too Fast
knownIssues.detail: When loading a Rivian onto a flatbed with Park brake release active, pull slowly and steadily. If you pull the vehicle too fast, it will automatically shift back to Park, stopping the load. Pull at a walking pace.

knownIssues.title: Park Brake Release Times Out After 15 Minutes
knownIssues.detail: The Park brake release function automatically turns off after 15 minutes. If you need more time, re-enable it via the touchscreen. You can also disable it by shifting back to Park or turning off the setting in the center display.

vehicles.slot: Electronic selector — touchscreen or physical button on console
shift: PREFERRED: Turn vehicle to ON/Ready mode.
Touchscreen — Settings > Vehicle > Service > Park brake release.
Enable Park brake release.
Release the brake and confirm the electronic park brake disengages.
Load onto flatbed — pull slowly (pulling too fast causes auto-return to Park).
DEAD 12V BATTERY:
12V battery is under the PASSENGER SEAT in the cab — lift the seat cushion.
Alternatively, a jump harness may be accessible behind the trailer hitch cover.
Connect jump pack to 12V terminals.
Once powered, use touchscreen Park brake release.
If no power: lift the rear wheels — EPB is rear-only.
neutral: FLATBED ONLY — electric drivetrain.
12V battery is under the PASSENGER SEAT in the cab.
To access: move passenger seat back, lift the seat cushion to expose battery terminals.
Connect jump pack. 12V AUXILIARY ONLY — NEVER touch HV battery.
Once powered, use Settings > Vehicle > Service > Park brake release.
Dead battery fallback: lift rear wheels (EPB is rear-only) to load onto flatbed.
vehicles.notes: Amazon/Rivian commercial delivery van. RWD electric. 12V battery is under the cab seat. VERY common commercial fleet tow. Flatbed only.
vehicles.warn: FLATBED ONLY. 12V battery under cab seat — NOT under the hood. Never touch HV battery.
towNotes: 12V battery is under the driver or passenger seat in the cab — NOT under the hood.
Very common fleet vehicle — operators will see this regularly.

knownIssues.title: 12V Battery Under Cab Seat — NOT Under Hood
knownIssues.detail: The Rivian EDV delivery van 12V auxiliary battery is under the cab seat (driver or passenger side depending on build), not under the hood. Lift the seat cushion to access it. Many operators waste time looking under the hood.
